paper.title: SayNav: Grounding Large Language Models for Dynamic Planning to Navigation in New Environments
paper.central_claim: Incrementally grounding an LLM in an explored 3D scene graph enables dynamic MultiON planning in unknown large houses, outperforming the privileged PointNav baseline (64.34% vs 56.06%) with a sample-efficient low-level policy.

evidence.quote: The observations include RGBD images, semantic segmentation maps, and the agent’s pose (location and orientation).
evidence.support_explanation: Semantic segmentation and pose are supplied observations, not a demonstrated raw-RGB perception system.

evidence.quote: For instance, we constrain each step to generate a navigate or look function call with arguments and a high-level comment.
evidence.support_explanation: Fixed typed calls connect LLM-generated plans to the executor.

evidence.quote: This low-level planner is trained from scratch (without pretraining) on only 2800 episodes or 7\times 10^{5} simulation steps.
evidence.support_explanation: The LLM is frozen but the PointNav executor is trained with oracle demonstrations.

evidence.quote: We build a benchmark dataset of 132 episodes using 132 different houses with 3-10 rooms each and select 3 objects for each house to conduct MultiON task.
evidence.support_explanation: Simulation evaluation denominator and house scale.

evidence.quote: SayNav, without using any ground truth, achieves a higher SR ( 60.32\% and 64.34\% with gpt-3.5-turbo and gpt-4 respectively).
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported VO/PNav results; their no-ground-truth phrasing must be read alongside supplied semantic segmentation.

evidence.quote: Looking at the SPL metric, we see a drop in SayNav as compared to the baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: Success improves, but path efficiency does not dominate the baseline.

evidence.quote: We do observe substantial drop in SR and SPL metrics by using LLM Memory in the case of gpt-3.5-turbo as compared to the results reported in Table 1 .
evidence.support_explanation: Memory effect depends on backbone; it is not a universal gain.

evidence.quote: The demonstration video for a cafeteria environment is available at our project link.
evidence.support_explanation: Real-robot evidence is a qualitative demonstration, not counted transfer trials.

evidence.quote: In the future, we would like to develop verification and feedback mechanisms to validate the plans generated by LLMs for improving SayNav’s performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Plan validation remains future work; scene-graph door-state errors cause failures.
Direct SR/SPL and privileged sensing/executor arms; baseline is not an upper bound on local waypoint organization.

signatures.output: Short-range PointNav targets and look actions
signatures.conditions: Static houses; visible/segmentable objects; reachable open doors; learned short-range executor.
signatures.feedback: New observations, found-object list and explored-door/room annotations
signatures.selection_rule: Current-room object likelihood/feasibility prioritization; no persistent harness edit acceptance.
signatures.selection_data: Current episode observations; fixed few-shot examples where specified. No claim of accepted cross-task harness edits.
signatures.persistence: Episode-local 3D graph and investigated-room flags; no cross-episode optimizer.
signatures.later_use: Later planning calls in the same episode read the graph.
signatures.claimed_effect: MultiON SR increase with less low-level training.
signatures.failure_boundary: Small objects, glass doors, open-door visibility; privileged sensing assumptions; long-range baseline differs structurally.

gap.author_gap: Prior LLM planners use small/known spaces or static whole-task plans; unknown multi-room MultiON requires online semantic exploration.
gap.checked_gap: The fixed text distinguishes full GT SayPlan scene graphs from incremental exploration and L3MVN frontier hints from step-by-step planning; this is a concrete interface/planning residual.

claims.text: SayNav raises MultiON success over a privileged PointNav baseline.
claims.setting: 132 houses, three targets, simulator semantic labels and pose.
claims.baseline/control: Same IL PointNav policy used for long-range GT-target baseline; SayNav uses local subgoals.
claims.selection_vs_test: Executor train split is separate; val/test pooled and harness-tuning separation not audited.
claims.result/denominator: GPT-4 VO/PNav SR 64.34% vs baseline 56.06%; SPL 0.33 vs 0.49 (Table 1).
claims.counterevidence: Baseline is not the same local-planning organization; oracle label does not make it an upper bound.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Descriptive increase on this dataset under supplied sensing, not isolated proof of superior LLM reasoning.

claims.result/denominator: Qualitative video only; no trial denominator.
claims.counterevidence: No hardware rates; semantic perception differs from simulator.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Demonstration feasibility only, not measured transfer.
